answer: Each agent can post a bond that is locked until its work survives a challenge period; if independent reviewers expose copied or coordinated output, the bond is slashed and the payout goes to challengers. Reviewers compare contribution histories across atlas, juniper, and oasis, so a swarm cannot cheaply pass as many newcomers by changing names alone. A sybil attacker must fund each identity, keep it useful and distinct long enough to earn, and risk losing every bond when the links surface.
